title: Samsung MagicINFO Flaw Used to Deploy AnyDesk and Compile Stealthy Cryptominer Payloads
content_md: Attackers exploited a known Samsung MagicINFO flaw to install remote-access software and build a Monero cryptominer directly on a victim’s Windows endpoint. The unusual build process created a burst of activity that made the attack easier to spot in endpoint telemetry. Huntress detected the activity in early September 2026 on a system running Samsung MagicINFO Premium, software used to manage digital signage. Researchers linked the initial access to CVE-2025-4632, a path traversal flaw that allows arbitrary files to be written with SYSTEM authority. Samsung fixed the vulnerability in May 2025; MagicINFO 9 Server versions before 21.1052 are affected. The endpoint generated another alert eight days after the first incident report. Huntress tied the new activity to the same access route. Process evidence showed commands running through tomcat9.exe , the Apache Tomcat service used by MagicINFO, helping analysts trace the activity back to the compromised application. MagicINFO Flaw Fuels Cryptomining The attacker tried three times to download AnyDesk from 194.87.89[.]30 . Microsoft Defender blocked the first attempt, which used certutil.exe , and the second, which used PowerShell’s Invoke-WebRequest . The third attempt succeeded. The attacker installed AnyDesk, set a password, and created a local account named oldadministrator using the same password. They then used SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe to disable Microsoft Defender. Detection of AnyDesk being downloaded (Source: huntress)

CVE-2025-4632.evidence: Attackers exploited the known MagicINFO flaw to install AnyDesk and compile a Monero miner on victim Windows endpoints, per observed intrusions.
